page: Microsoft Azure L64ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a 64-core ARM64 processor architecture with dedicated vCPU allocation. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 512 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not integrate discrete graphics accelerators, focusing resources entirely on core compute execution, high memory capacity, and high-throughput I/O pipelines.

Storage capability is anchored by 15,359 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, providing direct low-latency disk access for data-intensive operations alongside Premium Storage support. Because the compute environment relies on 64-bit ARM architecture, deployments require compatible operating systems and software binaries compiled for ARM64. Software stacks relying specifically on x86 instruction extensions or hardware-specific acceleration flags are not supported on this platform.

In terms of hardware allocation, the combination of ARM processor cores and dense local NVMe storage delivers high resource consolidation without the overhead of external storage networking. This configuration fits high-throughput transactional and NoSQL database engines, distributed caching clusters, large-scale data warehousing, real-time analytics, and data pipeline processing tasks that demand high local disk capacity and substantial memory reserves.
description: Microsoft Azure L64ps_v5 is a storage-optimized instance built on the ARM64 architecture, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The virtual machine provides 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 512 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-intensive computations. A central hardware characteristic is its bundled 15,359 GB local NVMe SSD storage tier, designed to handle high-throughput, low-latency disk I/O operations without depending solely on remote volumes. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs, directing its resources entirely toward data processing and storage throughput. Due to its ARM-based foundation, workloads must support ARM64 execution environments. By pairing high-density local NVMe capacity with power-efficient ARM compute, the L64ps_v5 delivers strong resource density for data-heavy systems. Recommended deployment scenarios include large-scale NoSQL and relational database deployments, real-time analytics engines, log analytics platforms, distributed file stores, and big data processing pipelines requiring substantial local storage buffers.
